newsitem.title: INDIA: South Asian nations to expand trade concessions.
newsitem.headline: South Asian nations to expand trade concessions.

text.p: Seven South Asian countries will conclude a second round of negotiations on tariff concessions in November, a senior Indian government official said on Tuesday.
Commerce Secretary Tejendra Khanna said some 1,200 products would be eligible for tariff concessions after next month's meeting. At present some 400 items are entitled for concessions.

"At the end of the second round we will definitely cross the 1,200 mark," Khanna told reporters after the third meeting of the inter-governmental group (ICG) on trade liberalisation, under South Asian Preferential Trade Agreement (SAPTA), in the Indian capital.
Seven nations - India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Maldives and Sri Lanka - form the South Asian Association of Regional Cooperation (SAARC).
The ICG will meet in Kathmandu, capital of Nepal, to conclude the trade negotiations, Khanna said.
The recommendations of the group will be forwarded for approval to a council of ministers of the SAARC.
SAARC launched SAPTA last year as a goal for creating a regional free-trade area.
"There is a willingness to move forward on trade concessions among SAARC nations," Khanna said.
He said given the willingness among the SAARC nations, the SAARC Free Trade Area (SAFTA) will be possible by the year 2000.
